# Architecture

## Engine choice

[PixiJS](https://pixijs.com/8.x/guides/components/application) supplies the WebGL renderer and scene graph. The game does not need a rigid-body physics engine, a tile map, or an entity framework: the recovered simulation uses authored tank parts, point-against-art collision, independent velocity axes, and frame timers. Keeping those rules in plain TypeScript avoids coupling them to a framework's physics or variable-time integration.

Next.js supplies the application shell, TypeScript build, and static delivery. Tailwind is installed through its PostCSS integration; stage-specific styling is kept in one stylesheet so original Flash coordinates can remain explicit. Pixi is imported on demand by rendered screens. No server-side game API or database is required.

## Ownership and flow

1. `AssetGate` accepts a local file or initializes procedural mock artwork.
2. `AssetPack` extracts images, sounds, vectors, font outlines, and sprite placements. It composes frozen previews and shared vector-leaf textures. It never executes ABC/ActionScript or calls retired endpoints.
3. `GameShell` owns the local profile, screen navigation, dialogs, and a `World` instance.
4. `GameViewport` owns input listeners, a fixed-step accumulator, the Pixi renderer, and cleanup. Input is cleared on blur and gameplay pauses when hidden.
5. `World.step` advances one original game frame. `weapons.ts`, `projectiles.ts`, `actor-movement.ts`, `waves.ts`, and `tank.ts` implement separate systems. Beam contact, healer patient ownership, turret construction, and status callbacks/clocks are isolated in `beams.ts`, `healing.ts`, `turrets.ts`, and `status.ts`. Rendering and browser storage are absent from these rules.
6. `GameRenderer` positions the camera at the avatar, draws fields/entities/projectiles/pickups/effects, and updates `SwfSymbolView` display lists. `AssetPack` supplies matching animated alpha-mask hit tests.
7. React observes a revision counter, approximately ten updates per second at 50 FPS; it does not render every simulation frame.

`MainMenuMotion` belongs to each menu instance and advances on the shared `StageRuntime`. `MainMenuView` retains the supplied-SWF title and control clip trees through Settings/Credits visits; A stage-wide `MenuPointer` queries native retained geometry or procedural contours; DOM buttons retain keyboard access over the canvas. Per-frame rendering uses refs and stage subscriptions, while `GameShell` owns screen changes and the guarded overlay. A new menu instance resets its intro; closing a child pane preserves its title timeline.

`TankCreator.onLoad` passes its avatar/enemy mode and current limits to the local `TankViewer` screen. `GameShell` retains the editor return context and paused game viewport through that visit; the viewer's artwork and fades use the same stage clock. Selection constructs a fresh editor from the chosen design. Back reconstructs the current avatar or a new empty enemy, matching the recovered source routes. Viewer save/delete callbacks update the versioned local profile, and only completing the final guide page persists `tankViewerHelpSeen`. ## API

- Construct one `UpgradeMenuMotion` for each original upgrade-menu instance; retain it while its creator/viewer child is displayed.
- `advance()` advances one source stage frame and returns ordered commands. It does not perform world, DOM, bitmap or audio work.
- `counter`, `historyIndex`, `savedFrames`, `foregroundAlpha`, `closing`, `finished` expose the source presentation state. `foregroundAlpha` is the signed quantized DisplayObject getter; it can be negative. Clamp paint only.
- `beginClosing()` succeeds once for a displayed loaded offer. Call it only after the synchronous chosen-code/avatar/PlaceAvatar work succeeds. Actual offer readiness remains the caller's responsibility.
- `showChild('creator' | 'viewer')` and `returnToOffers()` preserve the clock/history/alpha. `advance()` continues during child visits. Viewer updates are emitted first, before bitmap or completion work.

- `save-bitmap(index)` then `blur-bitmap` describes source capture-before-blur, not recapturing the game. There are19 such pairs at source counters2..38. Setup owns the initial clean capture and its exact event-frame handoff.
- `restore-bitmap(index, written)` describes source-over draw of that saved bitmap. The first reverse slot is unwritten/transparent. Do not substitute replacement or clear the current capture.

Do not execute both paths. The test patch verifies the existing history seam through full opening/reversal.
- `write-foreground-alpha.value` is the raw Number assigned to all six clips; `.alpha` is its signed quantized getter. Fade viewers/loading/text/parts/build/search only, not the root shade, other static root content or saved bitmap.
- `attach-bottom-handlers` occurs at entry counter38 (normally39th Run), not on the38th increment. It does not enable cards: their original listeners attach independently when offers arrive.
- `finish` corresponds to Destroy's presentation completion. Parent integration owns mode restoration and menu removal. It is emitted after40 closing writes from a fully opened menu, on41st closing Run.
- An existing bottom handler may open a child during closing. The retained Run still finishes and removes the menu; the module deliberately preserves this ordering.
